messages:
ana_pm: Heads up — ACME legal said they won't sign until 99p chat latency <150ms for typical sessions. They want firm launch criteria. Need to scope/prioritize for next two sprints.

mike_eng: Ack. Current 99p for 2k-token flows on hosted is ~420ms. Quick sketch of options: 1) small-model routing (fast, low effort), 2) KV prefetch + prefix cache (medium effort), 3) batching kernel work (higher effort), 4) quantized variant + distillation (risky for quality), 5) dedicated pool for ACME (expensive ops).

jess_ml: Impact: ACME ARR ~1.2M, strategic reference customer. If we get them, likely 3 more similar deals in pipeline. Risk: quantization can affect hallucination and can be hard to test across prompt families.

lucas_prod: Trying RICE on the fly for KV prefetch: Reach=6 (ACME + similar), Impact=8, Confidence=0.6, Effort=3 (sprint-weeks) -> Score ~ (6*8*0.6)/3 = 9.6. Small-model routing: Reach=8, Impact=6, Confidence=0.8, Effort=1 -> ~38.4. Batching infra: Reach=9, Impact=7, Confidence=0.5, Effort=6 -> ~10.5.

prabha_sre: Ops notes — dedicated pool reduces latency variance but increases monthly cost. Also need fallback policies so if pool is saturated we don't fail ACME traffic. We should define SLOs + rollback window.

mike_eng: For sequencing I suggest: 1) small-model routing + request routing rules (1w) 2) KV prefetch & prefix cache (2w) 3) batching heuristics & kernel tuning (4w) 4) quant variant behind FF + evals (3w) 5) dedicated pool if residual gap. Quick wins first to reduce tail.

ana_pm: (typo) ana_pm: +1 to that sequence. Can we make launch criteria concrete? Proposing: - Metric: 99th percentile end-to-end response latency <150ms on ACME traffic for chat sessions (post-auth); - Quality: no >2% regression on ACME prompt eval set; - Observability: dashboard, 5min alerts, and automatic rollback.

jess_ml: For quality gating we need an eval harness run on canary traffic. I can add a continuous eval that runs 500 prompts per minute and reports micro-F1 / hallucination proxy.

mike_eng: Implementation notes: KV prefetch will require changes to routing and KV cache eviction. Example prometheus query I'll use to measure 99p during canary:
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{service=\"infer\",env=\"prod\"}[5m])) by (le))
```
Also will add a per-customer tag to track ACME slice.

prabha_sre: Rollout plan: canary 2% traffic for 24h -> 10% for 48h -> 100% with monitoring. If 99p exceeds 150ms or eval regression >2% at any step, auto rollback. I'll own the automation.

lucas_prod: Cost tradeoff: routing + KV prefetch likely minimal infra cost. Batching kernel work reduces per-token cost long-term. Dedicated pool increases monthly cost but gives predictable tail. We should include cost runway in the decision (ACME prefers committed pricing).

mike_eng: One more thought: we can implement small-model routing as a policy that reduces ACME cost and tail latency immediately while enabling later improvements. That is highest RICE and lowest effort.

ana_pm: Decision proposal: prioritize small-model routing + KV prefetch in next sprint (ship quick wins), parallelize planning for batching work for sprint+1, start quant evaluation but gate behind FF, and only consider dedicated pool if after those steps 99p still >150ms. Anyone object? :thinking_face:

jess_ml: No objections. I'll start the eval harness and share prompt set.

mike_eng: I'll create tickets and estimate story points.

prabha_sre: I'll stub canary automation and cost estimate for dedicated pool.

lucas_prod: I'll update the roadmap doc and RICE table, include ACME ARR and confidence ranges, and link in the PRD.

deploy-bot: Note: scheduled maintenance window 2024-06-10 03:00 UTC — avoid major rollouts then.

ana_pm: Great — thanks everyone. I'll post the PRD draft with proposed launch criteria and sequencing later today. :rocket:
